interest: Shows Vichy Morocco romanticizing Japanese Bushido and Shinto to sway youth from Franco-American ties before Operation Torch.
overview: Despatch No. 692 (1942): Consul Russell forwards a Vichy youth magazine article romanticizing Japanese Bushido and Shinto, citing Emperor Meiji's rescript and Nitobe to win Moroccan youth from Franco-American ties.

people.name: Pierre Cordier
people.role: Collaborationist attached to the Sécurité Publique at Rabat

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a translation of a collaborationist youth newspaper article along with an assessment of pro-Axis and pro-Japanese propaganda efforts in French Morocco.
subfiles.from: H. Earle Russell, American Consul General, Casablanca
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 692: Russell warns Moroccan youth press glorifies Japan and the Axis, citing a Jeunesse article by Pierre Cordier.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 692 from H. Earle Russell (Casablanca) on Axis and Japanese Propaganda in Moroccan Youth Publications

subfiles.about: English translation of a collaborationist article extolling Japan's theocratic imperial governance, martial culture, and ethos of total self-sacrifice.
subfiles.summary: Cordier's Jeunesse article praises Japan's church-state unity under the Emperor, citing Meiji's Rescript to romanticize suicide attacks over Western individualism.
subfiles.title: Translation of Article "Japan Wins Its Battles by Its Established System of Church and State" by Pierre Cordier in "Jeunesse"
